$comment: Provenance: read from courier at a8f15ccef11bd6148c71fbe38327d9fbebbfe2e2, from `Courier.Events.bounced/1` in lib/courier/events.ex. The builder's own doc names this file and says the four fields are `message_id` / `user_id` / `notification_type` / `email`, "exactly as core/schemas/events/courier/email/bounced.schema.json requires". Written by `Courier.InboundReports` in the same transaction as the suppression row. The commit is fleet.yml's sourceCommit for courier.
title: courier.email.bounced payload
description: The `data` payload of the `courier.email.bounced` event: the destination hard-bounced. courier's manifest declares this type before it has a provider webhook to receive one, so the payload is the same four fields `courier.email.delivered` carries — enough to identify the notification that failed — and no provider diagnostic. A provider's bounce code is not a field here because no publisher emits one; it arrives with the receiver, and a new optional field is a patch. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

message_id.description: The notification that bounced. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`, and read back out of the `Message-ID` header the send set. Suppressing an address needs the address; un-sending a message needs this.

user_id.description: The user the message was for. A uuid from identity, not a cafaye-prefixed id: see D7.

notification_type.description: Which of courier's three messages bounced. A bounced address suppresses every type, so this is for a consumer that wants to know what the user missed rather than what to stop sending.

email.description: The address that bounced. The hard-bounce suppression list is keyed on this.
